lessons.title: أكبر من (akbar min) — bigger than
lessons.gloss: bigger than — the comparative shape aCCaC with min, the same shape with al- or before a noun for 'the biggest', and afḍal, better

segments.text: Say "it was a new experience", then "I hope to travel". (Kānat tajribatan jadīda, atamannā an usāfira.)
To describe an experience well, you set it beside another: the city or the village, the train or the bus.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: the shape aCCaC, and min

segments.text: Take the three root letters of a describing word and pour them into the shape a-C-C-a-C: kabīr, big, becomes أكبر akbar, bigger; ṣaghīr becomes aṣghar; sarīʿ, fast, becomes asraʿ. من — min, "from" — is the "than":
المدينة أكبر من القرية. — al-madīna akbar min al-qarya — The city is bigger than the village.

The shape does not change for a feminine noun: al-madīna akbar, al-qiṭār asraʿ min ad-darrāja. You have owned two of these since chapter one hundred and seventy-six: akthar, more, is the shape of kathīr, many, and aqall, less, of qalīl, few.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: the biggest, and better

segments.text: Put al- on it for "the biggest": al-akbar. Or set it before a noun with no article: أكبر مدينة akbar madīna, the biggest city.
"Better" has a shape of its own: أفضل afḍal, from the root of faḍḍala, to prefer, and of min faḍlik.
القطار أفضل من الحافلة. — al-qiṭār afḍal min al-ḥāfila — The train is better than the bus.
Al-afḍal is "the best".

segments.instruction: kabīr … akbar; ṣaghīr … aṣghar; sarīʿ … asraʿ
"The city is bigger than the village" — al-madīna akbar min al-qarya
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "The city is bigger than the village" — *al-madīna akbar min al-qarya*]

segments.instruction: "The train is faster than the bicycle" — al-qiṭār asraʿ min ad-darrāja
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "The train is faster than the bicycle" — *al-qiṭār asraʿ min ad-darrāja*]

segments.instruction: "I think the train is faster" — aʿtaqidu anna al-qiṭāra asraʿ
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "I think the train is faster" — *aʿtaqidu anna al-qiṭāra asraʿ*]

segments.instruction: "The train is better than the bus" — al-qiṭār afḍal min al-ḥāfila
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "The train is better than the bus" — *al-qiṭār afḍal min al-ḥāfila*]

segments.text: "Bigger than"? (Akbar min.) "Smaller"? (Aṣghar.) "The best"? (Al-afḍal.) Which two words were in this shape all along? (Akthar and aqall.)

lessons.title: منذ ثلاث سنوات (mundhu thalāth sanawāt) — for three years
lessons.gloss: for three years, three years ago — mundhu with the present for what is still going on, and qabla with a span for 'ago'

segments.text: Say "the city is bigger than the village", then "the biggest city". (Al-madīna akbar min al-qarya, akbar madīna.)
An experience also has a length. Mundhu, from chapter two hundred and thirty-three, measures it.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: mundhu and the present

segments.text: For something that began in the past and is still going on, Arabic keeps the present and adds mundhu with the span:
أعمل هنا منذ ثلاث سنوات. — aʿmalu hunā mundhu thalāth sanawāt — I have been working here for three years.
English says "have been working"; Arabic says "I work, since three years". With a point in time instead of a span, mundhu is "since": anā hunā mundhu aṣ-ṣabāḥ, I've been here since the morning.

Counting takes care. Sana, a year, ends in ة, and three to ten take the opposite ending to their noun: thalāth sanawāt, three years, but thalāthat ashhur, three months. For two, the noun takes -ayn: sanatayn, two years; usbūʿayn, two weeks.
For a finished event, use the past and قبل — qabla, "before" — with the span:
وصلت قبل أسبوع. — waṣaltu qabla usbūʿ — I arrived a week ago.
Mundhu with a past verb can say "ago" too: waṣaltu mundhu usbūʿ. With the present it can only mean "for".

segments.instruction: "I have been working here for three years" — aʿmalu hunā mundhu thalāth sanawāt
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "I have been working here for three years" — *aʿmalu hunā mundhu thalāth sanawāt*]

segments.instruction: "for three months", then "for two weeks" — mundhu thalāthat ashhur, mundhu usbūʿayn
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "for three months", then "for two weeks" — *mundhu thalāthat ashhur*, *mundhu usbūʿayn*]

segments.instruction: "I arrived a week ago" — waṣaltu qabla usbūʿ
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "I arrived a week ago" — *waṣaltu qabla usbūʿ*]

segments.instruction: "I have known my friend for two years" — aʿrifu ṣadīqī mundhu sanatayn
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "I have known my friend for two years" — *aʿrifu ṣadīqī mundhu sanatayn*]

segments.instruction: how long you have lived where you live — askunu hunā mundhu …
segments.source: [YOU SAY: how long you have lived where you live — *askunu hunā mundhu …*]

segments.text: "For three years", with a present? (Mundhu thalāth sanawāt.) "A week ago"? (Qabla usbūʿ.) "Two years"? (Sanatayn.) Which tense goes with mundhu for "for"? (The present.)

lessons.title: Review — bigger, better, and for how long
lessons.gloss: an experience set beside another and measured — akbar min, al-afḍal, mundhu with the present, qabla for 'ago'

segments.text: Say "I was happy" and "I felt afraid". (Kuntu saʿīdan, shaʿartu bi-l-khawf.) Then "I want to become an engineer". (Urīdu an uṣbiḥa muhandisan.)

Two lessons, and an experience can be weighed and measured. Weighed with the shape aCCaC and min: akbar min, asraʿ min, afḍal min; with al- or before a noun for the most: al-afḍal, akbar madīna. Measured with mundhu and the present, for what is still going on, and qabla with the past, for "ago".
Both in one breath:
سافرت بالطائرة قبل سنة، وكانت أفضل تجربة. — sāfartu bi-ṭ-ṭāʾira qabla sana, wa-kānat afḍala tajriba — I travelled by plane a year ago, and it was the best experience.

segments.instruction: "The plane is faster than the train" — aṭ-ṭāʾira asraʿ min al-qiṭār
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "The plane is faster than the train" — *aṭ-ṭāʾira asraʿ min al-qiṭār*]

segments.instruction: "The pencil case is smaller" — al-miqlama aṣghar
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "The pencil case is smaller" — *al-miqlama aṣghar*]

segments.instruction: "I have been waiting for the information since the morning" — antaẓiru al-maʿlūmāt mundhu aṣ-ṣabāḥ
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "I have been waiting for the information since the morning" — *antaẓiru al-maʿlūmāt mundhu aṣ-ṣabāḥ*]

segments.instruction: something you did a year ago, and how long you have done something else
segments.source: [YOU SAY: something you did a year ago, and how long you have done something else]

segments.text: "Better than"? (Afḍal min.) "The best experience"? (Afḍal tajriba.) "For two years", with a present? (Mundhu sanatayn.) "A year ago"? (Qabla sana.)
